title: Understanding Pipe Sizing: Main Lines vs. Branch Lines
description: Pipe sizing directly controls both water flow rate and dynamic pressure. When a main supply line is undersized, turning on a single extra fixture causes a noticeable drop in flow elsewhere in the building. A properly sized main supply line—often 3/4-inch in standard residential supply—delivers the total volume required before stepping down to 1/2-inch branch lines for individual fixtures. This hierarchy prevents high velocity, noisy friction loss, and sudden pressure drops during concurrent use. Always consult local plumbing codes and fixture unit calculations when sizing supply lines for multi-fixture demand.

visual_story: The image focuses on the physical size reduction where a 3/4-inch main copper trunk line feeds smaller 1/2-inch branch lines. Viewers can easily see the visual distinction between the main supply pipe diameter and the fixture branch pipes. This visual reinforces the concept of fluid hierarchy, showing that main supply lines must carry larger volume capacity to serve smaller individual branches without restricting total system flow.

on_image_text.hook: Why Pipe Size Controls Your Water Pressure
on_image_text.explanation: Undersized main lines increase friction loss and cause severe pressure drops during concurrent fixture use.
on_image_text.takeaway: Size main supply trunks to support total fixture demand before branching off.
